official.description_text:
Doctoral student in Machine Learning for Integrated Resources Modelling
Apply for position
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Industrial Engineering and Management
Project description
Third-cycle subject:
Energy and Environmental Systems
The division of Energy Systems (dES) within the Department of Energy Technology at KTH has been driving the advancement of energy systems and integrated resource assessment methodologies for supporting integrated resource planning in developed and developing countries, through funding from UK Aid, UN and European Union. The division is now hiring a PhD student who shall work on a step change in the methodologies by using Machine Learning, whose benefits will cut across these funding streams. The student’s work will focus on using ML to generate workflows that enable the exploration of uncertainties and of wide scenario spaces in large and granular bottom-up integrated resource models. This shall support fit-for-context modelling in chosen developed and developing contexts that the division works in. Travels and engagement with government and stakeholders in the selected contexts and participation in capacity development activities will be part of the regular tasks of the student.
Supervision:
Francesco Gardumi is proposed to supervise the doctoral student. Decisions are made on admission
Admission requirements
To be admitted to postgraduate education (Chapter 7, 39 § Swedish Higher Education Ordinance), the applicant must have basic eligibility in accordance with either of the following:
passed a second cycle degree (for example a master's degree), or
completed course requirements of at least 240 higher education credits, of which at least 60 second-cycle higher education credits, or
acquired, in some other way within or outside the country, substantially equivalent knowledge
In addition to the above, there is also a
mandatory requirement for English equivalent to English B/6.
Selection
In order to succeed as a doctoral student at KTH you need to be goal oriented and persevering in your work. During the selection process, candidates will be assessed upon their ability to:
independently pursue his or her work
collaborate with others,
have a professional approach and
analyze and work with complex issues.
You should also have good knowledge of energy technology and integrated resource systems, as well as modeling within the field, including data processing and Machine Learning techniques.
You shall be able to engage and collaborate with external partners and stakeholders in Sweden and abroad.
After the qualification requirements, great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Target degree: Doctoral degree
Information regarding admission and employment
Only those admitted to postgraduate education may be employed as a doctoral student. The total length of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education in four years' time. An employed doctoral student can, to a limited extent (maximum 20%), perform certain tasks within their role, e.g. training and administration. A new position as a doctoral student is for a maximum of one year, and then the employment may be renewed for a maximum of two years at a time. In the case of studies that are to be completed with a licentiate degree, the total period of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education for two years.
As a doctoral student, you are entitled to a workplace with
many employee benefits
and monthly salary according to
KTH’s Doctoral student salary agreement
. Read more about

To apply for the position
Apply for the position and admission through KTH's recruitment system. It is the applicant’s responsibility to ensure that the application is complete in accordance with the instructions in the advertisement.
Applications must include the following elements:
Copies of diplomas and grades from previous university studies and certificates of fulfilled
language requirements (see above)
. Translations into English or Swedish if the original document is not issued in one of these languages.Copies of originals must be
certified
.
CV including your relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Application letter with a brief description of why you want to pursue research studies, about what your academic interests are and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. (Maximum 2 pages long)
Representative publications or technical reports. For longer documents, please provide a summary (abstract) and a web link to the full text.
Applications must be received at the last closing date at midnight, CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).

In such cases, a prerequisite for employment is that the applicant is approved following the security clearance.
We firmly decline all contact with staffing and recruitment agencies and job ad salespersons.

ai.summary: Doctoral position at KTH in machine learning for energy systems modelling. Focus on using ML to explore uncertainties and scenario spaces in large bottom-up integrated resource models, with stakeholder engagement in developed and developing contexts.

thematic_fit.rationale: Position addresses energy systems, resource modelling, and policy support for energy planning. No mention of spatial cognition, immersive learning, wayfinding, collaborative immersive systems, or human-centred design. Completely orthogonal to candidate's research domains.

methodological_fit.rationale: Posting emphasises machine learning, data processing, large-scale modelling, and stakeholder engagement in international contexts. Candidate has user-studies and beginner Python skills but no background in energy systems, resource modelling, or ML for domain-specific simulation. Stakeholder engagement is the only methodological thread; insufficient overlap.

growth_value.rationale: Would develop machine-learning application in energy systems, data processing, and international stakeholder collaboration—valuable for systems-thinking maturity but unrelated to spatial cognition, immersive-system design, or learning-transfer research. Does not advance target research identity.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH in Sweden is target geography; stable 4-year funding with international engagement (capacity-building, government partnerships). However, energy systems discipline and policy-support focus place candidate outside human-centred HCI/XR community. Supervision by energy-systems researchers; unfamiliar research culture.

eligibility_flags: Requires MSc (degree held) or equivalent; candidate is MSc by Research in progress.
Position requires good knowledge of energy technology, integrated resource systems, and modelling within the field—candidate has none.
Posting emphasises data processing and ML techniques for energy systems; candidate has no energy-domain background.
International travel and stakeholder engagement in energy-planning contexts (government, UN, UK Aid partners)—not immersive-systems research.
No mention of spatial cognition, learning, immersive interaction, or collaborative design.
risks: Thematic misalignment with spatial cognition and immersive learning; energy systems is orthogonal domain.
Significant domain-knowledge gap in energy technology and systems modelling.
Python skill is beginner-level; ML work would require substantial foundational development.
International field engagement in energy policy contexts may distance candidate from HCI/XR research community.
4-year commitment in energy systems would delay PhD in target domain.
Supervision by energy-systems researchers; unfamiliar discipline culture.
